scenes.headline: How to pause a C function mid-loop and resume it
scenes.sub: Simon Tatham's coroutines: a switch statement and __LINE__.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Gadget! C has no coroutines. But with one switch statement and one macro, you can fake them. Here's how.

scenes.text: On the way out, save the line number. On the way back in, switch on it, and a case label inside the loop resumes you exactly there.
scenes.mark: a case label inside the loop
scenes.say: On the way out, save the line number. On the way back, switch on it, and land on a case label inside the loop.

left.title: Hand-rolled state machine
items: Rip out the loop, hoist locals into static state
Every return needs its own number and case
left.say: Two loops that both want to call. Make one a callee by hand, and it turns into a numbered state machine.

right.title: A coroutine
items: Return from the middle, resume there later
Faked with a switch and one macro
right.say: A coroutine returns from the middle, and resumes right there later.

scenes.title: The whole trick, in one macro
scenes.say: The preprocessor already numbers every position: the line number. The return macro does three things.

parts.note: stamp the current line number into state
parts.say: It saves the current line into state.

parts.note: hand the value back, like any function
a label on the same line, for the way back in
parts.say: And it plants a case label with that same number.

items.say: First call: state is zero, so the switch enters at case zero.
The macro stamps its line into state, and returns zero.

items.text: Next call: jump into the loop
items.say: Next call, the switch jumps to the label inside the loop. The static counter survived, so it returns one.
Then two. Then the loop ends: minus one.

steps.say: One catch: static means one shared copy. Two callers would stomp on each other.
The fix: move the state and every serious local into a struct the caller owns.

steps.note: a hundred independent generators at once
steps.say: Now each caller has its own, and a hundred can run at once.

scenes.text: A coroutine is just a state machine where the compiler tracks the state for you.
scenes.mark: the compiler tracks the state for you

recap: Switch back to a case label mid-loop
Put the state in a struct for reentrancy
scenes.say: To recap: save the line, switch back to it, and keep the state in a struct.
